candidates.name: Jinpukaku
candidates.reason: Closed for preservation/renovation work from Dec 29 2023 for approximately five years (exterior covered as of Sep 2025); only the Horyu-in garden and Hosen-an teahouse on the grounds remain open, so it does not survive as a standalone stop during this trip's window.

candidates.name: Kanikichi
candidates.reason: Tourist-oriented crab specialist in central Tottori city; also moot for this trip's Oct 20-23 window since matsuba-gani (the marquee Tottori crab) season does not open until Nov 6 — see disagreement d-crab-season.

candidates.name: Iwamoto Shokudo
candidates.reason: Well-regarded Kurayoshi yoshoku (Tottori wagyu x pork hamburger steak) spot that cleared discovery, but redundant with the wagyu pick already shipped for the trip's one Kurayoshi dinner slot; kept as a lead for a future/longer visit rather than shipped.

candidates.name: 20th Century Pear Museum
candidates.reason: Thin connection to the trip's two ranked priorities (culture/history, food); a nashi-pear museum stop trades time against the Sanbutsu-ji climb window and the party's limited-mobility pace budget for a low payoff.

candidates.name: Mount Daisen
candidates.reason: Roughly 90 minutes-2 hours outside the compact Tottori-Kurayoshi-Misasa loop the trip is built around; would consume a full day the 4-day, balanced-pace itinerary does not have.

evidence.claim: Hinomaru Bus's (72)(73) Misasa Line connects Kurayoshi Station and Misasa Onsen on the schedule effective April 1, 2025 (current as of this pass).

Weekday downbound (Kurayoshi toward Misasa) departures run roughly hourly through the morning, then thin to gaps of up to ~100 minutes in early afternoon (12:22 to 14:04), with the last weekday departure at 19:08.

Weekday upbound (Misasa toward Kurayoshi/Ikuta depot) service thins in the evening; the last recorded weekday departure from the Misasa-area stops (Misasa depot / Onsen South Exit) is around 18:03-18:04.

Misasa Onsen's own tourism portal describes the JR Kurayoshi Station to Misasa Onsen connection as approximately a 20-minute local bus ride, used for all listed rail routings (from Osaka, Tokyo, and Okayama alike).

The operator's own current fare table for this line exists only as a PDF; two fetch attempts returned unreadable binary content, so the exact current yen fare could not be confirmed from the primary source.

Limited express trains (Super Hakuto/Super Oki/Super Matsukaze) connect Tottori Station and Kurayoshi Station in about 30 minutes on the San'in Main Line; a local (non-express) train covers the same route in about 60 minutes.

JR West's own Tottori-Matsue area rail-pass page names Super Hakuto, Super Inaba, and Yakumo as limited express services covering this area, with non-reserved ordinary seats included on the relevant area pass — confirming these named services (rather than an invented one) are what a traveler will see on station boards.
The Tottori Sand Dunes themselves are free to enter with no admission fee; the dune-side visitor lots (e.g. the 180-car overlook lot) are free parking.
Sand Museum hours are 9:00-18:00 with last entry at 17:30; adult admission is ¥800.
The 17th exhibition period, themed Spain ("Sand World Travel: Spain"), runs April 24 2026 through January 3 2027 — so it will be on display during an Oct 20-23 2026 visit.
San'in Matsushima Yuran's standard sightseeing cruise runs March through November, departing hourly 9:30-15:30 (each cruise ~40 minutes); adult fare is ¥1,800.
The operator's own homepage confirms hourly 9:30-15:30 departures for the main cruise and tells visitors to confirm current conditions before visiting — cruises are weather-dependent and can cancel.

A separate general tourism spot page cites 'from ¥1,300' for boat options at this coast, lower than the ¥1,800 confirmed directly on the operator's own cruise-specific page — see disagreement d-cruise-fare.

The Shirakabe Dozo-gun district is reached from Kurayoshi Station by a city-route bus (~10-15 min) alighting at the Akagawara/Shirakabe-Dozogun stop, then a short walk; the district's tourist information center sits inside Akagawara Building No. 10, open 9:00-17:00.

Nageiredo climb admission is ¥1,200 adult (includes the ¥400 base temple fee); general temple admission without the climb is ¥400 adult. Reception is 8:00-15:00 with a 16:30 mandatory descent deadline. A minimum of two people is mandatory (no solo climbers); dedicated hiking-style footwear is required, and entry is prohibited in rain, snow, or other conditions the temple judges dangerous.

A free public viewing platform (Nageiredo Yohaijo) at the foot of Mitokusan was completed and dedicated in November 2022, roughly 600m from Nageiredo itself (partial view, obstructed by trees); it has designated accessible parking and lets visitors view the National Treasure hall without climbing and regardless of weather.

Jinpukaku entered long-term closure on Dec 29 2023 for approximately five years of preservation/restoration work; as of Sep 2025 the exterior is covered by construction sheeting. The Horyu-in garden and Hosen-an teahouse on the same grounds remain open, 9:00-17:00, closed Mondays.

Kabuyu public bath (Misasa Onsen's original source bath) is open 12:00-20:45 (last entry 20:15) in the late-spring/early-summer schedule listed, shifting to a 9:00 opening from June 2 onward per the same schedule; adult admission ¥400. An adjoining free footbath and drinking-spring station run daily except Mondays (footbath from 10:00 on Mondays).

Yakiniku Masashige Kurayoshi: dinner service 17:00-22:30 (L.O. 22:00) daily; lunch 11:30-14:30 weekends/holidays only. Closed weekday lunches, Dec 31, Jan 1. Private rooms seat 2-60 across the 116-seat restaurant. Four Tottori Wagyu course options at ¥2,800 / ¥3,800 / ¥5,500 / ¥6,600 per person.

The restaurant's own online reservation system tops out selectable party sizes below 8 and tells guests who can't select their real party size to call the shop directly — see disagreement d-masashige-party-size.
Matsuba-gani (male snow crab) season in Tottori/San'in opens Nov 6 2026 and runs through Mar 20 2027, fixed by national ministerial order — the season has not started during an Oct 20-23 2026 trip.

Beni-zuwaigani (red snow crab) season at Sakaiminato/Tottori runs Sept 1 through the following June 30, with fuller market availability from mid-to-late September onward — meaning it, not matsuba-gani, is the crab actually in season during an Oct 20-23 trip.

Menya Hachibee (麺屋八兵衛), a gyukotsu (beef-bone broth) ramen specialist in Kurayoshi (Fukuniwa-cho), founded 2009, signature ramen ¥780; local web coverage says it was once selected for the Michelin Guide. Hours and closed day could not be confirmed against a qualifying primary/operator source — see freshness flag.
US passport holders are visa-exempt for stays of 90 days or less for tourism under Japan's reciprocal exemption arrangement.

Japan MOFA's own visa-exemption page and the Japanese Consulate/Embassy pages returned HTTP 403 on every fetch attempt in this environment; japan.travel (JNTO, also an official Japanese-government tourism body) was used as the reachable official alternative for the entry-rules claim above.

Japan's emergency numbers are 110 (police) and 119 (fire/ambulance); the JNTO Japan Visitor Hotline (050-3816-2787, also reachable from overseas) runs 24/7 in English, Chinese, Korean, and Japanese and explicitly covers emergency support for illness and disasters, not just tourist information.

7-Eleven (Seven Bank) ATMs accept foreign Visa/Mastercard/Maestro/UnionPay/Amex 24 hours nationwide; Japan Post ATMs have the strongest rural coverage as a backup but run restricted hours (roughly 08:45-21:00 weekdays, shorter Saturdays, closed most Sundays). Convenience-store density drops in rural areas like the Kurayoshi/Misasa side of this trip.
Reference mid-market rate: 1 USD ≈ ¥159.4 (informational only — not the rate any card or exchange counter will actually give).

reservations.releaseWindow: Online: same day up to 1 month ahead. For a party of 8, the online form's party-size selector tops out below 8 (confirmed by direct fetch of the booking page) — the site tells guests in that case to contact the restaurant directly.
reservations.actionDate: Call ahead once dinner-night plans firm up (this trip: aim for the Day 2 Kurayoshi transit day, before the last Misasa-bound bus).
reservations.partyRules: Private rooms run 2-60 people across 116 total seats, so 8 is comfortably within capacity — the constraint is the online tool's selector cap, not the restaurant's real capacity.
reservations.foreignFriction: Online form is Japanese-only; phone (0858-26-2919) is the reliable path for a party of 8 and lets staff confirm a room that seats the whole group together.
reservations.walkIn: Possible off-peak given 116 total seats, but not guaranteed for a party of 8 without a reservation.
reservations.alternatives: Iwamoto Shokudo (yoshoku, Tottori wagyu x pork) is a considered-but-not-shipped backup — see candidate c-iwamoto-shokudo.
reservations.fallback: If the phone line can't seat 8 together, split into two adjoining private rooms (2-6 each) rather than losing the venue.

reservations.releaseWindow: No advance reservation system — same-day registration only, at the temple.
reservations.actionDate: Arrive by mid-morning: reception is 8:00-15:00 with a mandatory 16:30 descent deadline, and the climb itself typically runs 90-120 minutes round trip before accounting for queueing at the chain sections.
reservations.partyRules: Minimum two people per climbing group (no solo climbers, strictly enforced); footwear is inspected at the reception desk — dedicated hiking-style soles required, rental straw sandals (waraji) available as a substitute, sneakers may be turned away.
reservations.cancellation: Entry is refused outright in rain, snow, or any condition the temple judges dangerous — this is a same-day go/no-go call, not a bookable slot.
reservations.walkIn: Walk-in only; no reservation exists to lose.
reservations.alternatives: The free Nageiredo Yohaijo viewing platform (candidate c-mitokusan-nageiredo-viewing-platform) is the honest alternative for anyone in the party who can't or shouldn't attempt the climb — see the sights write-up.
reservations.fallback: If weather closes the mountain, fall back to the viewing platform plus the ¥400 main-hall (Sanbutsu-ji hondo) visit, which doesn't require the climb.

transport.route: Kurayoshi Station -> Misasa Onsen (Hinomaru Bus, Kamii-Misasa/Misasa Line, route 72/73)
transport.doorToDoor: From the Kurayoshi Station bus stop, the ride to the Misasa Onsen area stops (Onsen South Exit / Misasa Onsen Tourism Center) runs about 20-26 minutes depending on the exact drop-off.
transport.transferReality: A standard route bus (fare box, no reserved seating, boarding by the rear door in the usual Japan local-bus pattern) rather than a coach — there is no dedicated luggage hold, so suitcases ride in the aisle/legroom area.
transport.groupLuggageMobility: For 8 travelers including 2 with low walking tolerance and full luggage, this is materially different from a solo traveler's transfer: boarding with bags takes longer, the bus may not have 8 adjacent seats free, and standing with luggage on a winding rural road is a real fatigue cost for the low-mobility pair. Build the transfer around a bus that isn't near-empty-standing-room, not just the next departure.
transport.buffer: Weekday midday service has a gap of roughly 100 minutes (12:22-14:04) — missing a bus in that window is not a 10-minute inconvenience, it's an hour-plus wait with luggage and no seating guarantee at the stop.
transport.missedConnection: Missing the last practical evening bus (~19:08 downbound) leaves taxi as the only same-night option to Misasa.
transport.nextService: Outside the midday gap, the next departure is typically within 30-90 minutes on the schedule fetched for this pass.
transport.lastPracticalReturn: Last confirmed weekday downbound (Kurayoshi -> Misasa) departure: 19:08. Build the Day 2 dinner in Kurayoshi to end with a real buffer before that, not against it.
transport.fallback: Taxi, ~20 minutes: Nikko/Chuo Taxi (0858-22-7111) or Kurayoshi Kotsu (0858-22-1511). The only fare figure located (~¥2,880) is undated-to-2009 and unconfirmed for 2026 — treat it as an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a quoted price, and expect to need 2 taxis for a party of 8 with luggage.

disagreements.topic: Uradome Coast sightseeing cruise adult fare: ¥1,300 vs ¥1,800
disagreements.investigation: The operator's own cruise-specific page (fetched directly) states ¥1,800 for the standard/large sightseeing cruise. A separate, more general tourism-spot page from the same booking-agent domain states 'from ¥1,300', which reads as either a stale figure or a reference to a different/shorter boat option on the same coast rather than the standard cruise.
disagreements.resolution: Ship ¥1,800 as the confirmed adult fare for the standard cruise (the figure from the product-specific official page), and note in the guide that a cheaper short-boat option may exist at the dock — doesn't change which cruise the guide recommends.

disagreements.topic: Yakiniku Masashige Kurayoshi private-room capacity: 'up to 6' vs 'up to 60'
disagreements.investigation: A third-party booking aggregator summary said private rooms seat 2-6. The restaurant's own site (masashige55.com, fetched directly) states private rooms run 2-60 across 116 total seats. The online reservation widget (toreta.in, fetched directly) confirms its own party-size selector doesn't reach 8 and tells guests to call the shop directly in that case.
disagreements.resolution: The restaurant can genuinely seat a party of 8, but the self-service online booking tool cannot secure it — for this trip's group of 8, book by phone, not the web form. This is exactly the party-size feasibility decision the trip's food pick needed.

saturation.note: Later searches on both ranked priorities (additional crab restaurants, additional onsen bathhouses, further day-trip peaks/temples) kept surfacing the same handful of names or options that were clearly weaker/out-of-scope for a compact 4-day, balanced-pace, no-rental-car trip (Mount Daisen too far, generic central-Tottori crab chains both touristy and out of season). The two open threads — the bus fare PDF being unreadable, and Menya Hachibee's hours lacking a qualifying primary source — affect whether a couple of figures ship clean vs. flagged, not which candidates make the guide, so they don't block stopping. Pass B's independent native-language sweep is the next real chance to surface something this pass missed.
